text:
harper: FYI — shipping a customer PoC on Cloudflare Workers and hit a hard build error: esbuild fails with \"could not resolve 'fs'\" when importing `redwood-inference`. Anyone have a low-friction pattern so users don’t need to add `--external` flags?

zain: Common problem. Workers are browser-like — no Node builtins. We should provide a documented edge subpath (eg `redwood-inference/edge`) that only includes a fetch-based transport and DOM-friendly types.

harper: I hacked a quick fix in the app by adding this to wrangler build: `esbuild --platform=browser --external:fs --external:net --define:process.env.NODE_ENV='\"production\"'` but that’s not acceptable for docs.

cole: Short roadmap: 1) Add `./edge` export in package.json pointing to `dist/edge.mjs`. 2) Emit `dist/edge.d.ts` using lib.dom types (ReadableStream). 3) Ensure retry/backoff uses `globalThis.setTimeout` and no `process.nextTick`/`setImmediate`.

zain: Also add a small helper for randomness: `randomBytes(n)` implemented with `crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(n))` and return Uint8Array in edge types (no Buffer). Document the difference.

harper: Types issue I saw: even if we ship edge.d.ts, some TS consumers still pick up root index.d.ts. How to ensure edge consumers get edge types?

cole: Use package.json `exports` mapping for subpath with a `types` field and encourage the subpath import in docs: `import { createEdgeClient } from 'redwood-inference/edge'`. Optionally add `typesVersions` for older TS resolvers.

zain: For bundler UX, add a `browser` map to package.json to stub debug/logger in browser/edge bundles. That avoids pulling in transitive node modules. Also make the main entry lazy-load heavy dev deps with dynamic import so they don't end up in edge bundles.

harper: Good call. Any wrangler-specific quickstart we can add to docs so customers have a copy/paste solution?

wrangler-bot: Suggested snippet for docs — put this in the starter repo README:
```
# wrangler.toml
name = "my-worker"
main = "./dist/worker.js"

# build command
[build]
command = "esbuild src/index.ts --bundle --outfile=dist/worker.js --platform=browser --format=esm"

# src/index.ts
import { createEdgeClient } from 'redwood-inference/edge'
const client = createEdgeClient({ url: REDWOOD_URL, apiKey: REDWOOD_KEY })
addEventListener('fetch', e => e.respondWith(handle(e.request)))
async function handle(req){ const out = await client.generate({ prompt: 'hi' }); return new Response(out.text || JSON.stringify(out)) }
```
This assumes `redwood-inference` publishes an `/edge` export.

pkg-ci: CI note: branch `edge-subpath-proto` exists. Build produced `dist/edge.mjs` and `dist/edge.d.ts`. Unit tests: 70/72; two node-only tests skipped in the edge matrix.

zain: Docs: add a Troubleshooting bullet list: 1) If you see Node modules during bundling, prefer `redwood-inference/edge`. 2) If you must bundle main entry, use `--platform=browser` and `--external:fs`. 3) TS: ensure `lib` includes `dom`. 4) Avoid runtime `process.env` reads; pass config object instead.

harper: Also call out header size limits — do not send large debug JSON headers from edge client; gate verbose headers on an opt-in flag. We hit that during local testing.

zain: Telemetry: add an opt-in event when `createEdgeClient` is instantiated so we can measure adoption before removing heavy deps from the default entry. Keep it privacy-preserving and documented.

harper: I’ll draft the workers-starter repo with the snippet above and open a docs PR linking to the CI branch. Thanks, all — this unblocks the customer. :rocket:
